lines.text: Every business-development tool finds an announcement, decides it means somebody needs your product, and hands a salesperson a lead.
That middle step is a guess. It is usually wrong, and it is never shown to you.
So we built one that refuses. Twenty-five opportunities across ninety-eight accounts, every row carrying a quote, a source, and a reason it might be wrong.
The model has to return a verbatim quote. Then code searches the page we fetched for those exact words. This one is in the page. This one the model invented, so it is refused.
That rule came from auditing six collusion detectors with Apart Research. Two of them could not be told apart from a crowd of deliberately meaningless rivals.
So I pointed that standard at my own system, and added paraphrases of real sentences from the correct page. Forty-nine per cent of them passed. Five hundred and seventy-three tests never caught it.
On NEAR testnet, the worker delivered a paraphrase and tried to pay itself. The contract reverted it. The arbiter refunded the buyer.
Inference runs inside a NEAR enclave, and the system fetches its own attestation. We found our own flaw before a judge could.
